title: Beirut International Airport opens to visitors
why: Opened in 1954; it fed the boom that made Beirut the tourist capital of the region.

title: First Baalbeck International Festival season is organised
why: Roman ruins became an annual stage; the festival runs on and off to today.

title: Fairuz debuts at Baalbeck and is named Cavalier
why: The Rahbani brothers' voice of Lebanon starts her 60-year career as a national symbol.

title: Private TV begins in Lebanon (CLT, channels 7 and 9)
why: First TV station in the region, six hours a night, in Arabic and French.

title: Casino du Liban opens in Jounieh
why: Cabaret and gaming venue that drew Jacques Brel and Duke Ellington; closed 1989, reopened 1996 after $50m.

title: Phoenicia Intercontinental hotel opens in Beirut
why: A flagship of the golden-age hotel strip that sold Beirut to the jet set.

title: Lebanese Ski Federation founded; Cedars ski week from 1962
why: Start of about three decades of skiing glory; the Cedars hosted a yearly international ski week until 1975. Federation 1961 (one source 1960); international ski week 1962-1975.

title: Haigazian students launch Lebanon's first rocket
why: A student club put the first Arab-world rockets in the air; President Chehab funded it from 1962; last launch 1966.

title: Cedar IV rocket reaches a reported 140 km altitude
why: Headline claim of the Lebanese Rocket Society; altitude is as stated by the page, not independently checked.

title: Umm Kulthum sings at Baalbeck; Ella Fitzgerald follows in 1971, Miles Davis in 1973
why: The festival drew Arab and Western stars alike before the war paused it. Umm Kulthum 1966 (also 1968, 1970), Fitzgerald 1971, Davis 1973.

title: Georgina Rizk crowned Miss Universe in Miami Beach
why: First Lebanese and first Arab Miss Universe, and still the only one from the Arab world (per The National, unread).

title: Mohamed Kheir Tarabulsi wins weightlifting silver at Munich
why: One of Lebanon's four Olympic medals (two silver, two bronze through 2022, three in wrestling); the other silver came in 1952.

title: Tourist arrivals peak at 1.4 million
why: The last peak before the war; the number was only beaten again around 2009.

title: Hassan Bchara wins Olympic bronze in Greco-Roman wrestling
why: Lebanon's last Olympic medal as of 2016, won in the middle of the civil war, aged 35.

title: Lebanese pound passes 455 to the dollar
why: From about 2.3 in 1975; wartime collapse that made the dollar the household yardstick. IMF: 455 LBP/USD in 1987.

title: Pound hits 2,825 per dollar before the recovery
why: War-era trough; then a decade-long fall back to a peg. IMF: 2,825 LBP/USD in May 1992.

title: Cellis and LibanCell win ten-year mobile contracts
why: Two state-contracted GSM networks; by 2004 consumers were boycotting their tariffs. Two GSM contracts awarded June 1994 for ten years.

title: Casino du Liban reopens after $50 million restoration
why: Closed since 1989; reopened as a symbol of post-war normality.

title: Baalbeck Festival returns after 25 years
why: Reopened amid post-war reconstruction and kept running to the 2020s.

title: Pound pegged at 1,507.5 per dollar
why: A peg that held in the official window for 22 years; later prices in this timeline start from it.

title: Lebanon hosts the AFC Asian Cup
why: First-ever finals entry, as host; eliminated in round one after a 4-0 loss to Iran.

title: Lebanon reach their first FIBA Asia final, lose to China
why: Start of Lebanese basketball's golden run; runner-up again in 2005, 2007, 2022.

title: Lebanon play their first basketball World Championship
why: 0-5 record and 16th place in the US; they returned in 2006, 2010 and 2023 (no title: they never won a world championship).

title: First Beirut Marathon draws 6,000 runners from 49 countries
why: Created by May El-Khalil; 15,000 ran the 21st edition in 2025.

title: Consumers boycott mobile phones for 24 hours over tariffs
why: 500 minutes cost USD 121 in Lebanon against 39-66 in neighbours; mobile was the state's third-biggest revenue.

title: Lebanon withdraws from Eurovision over broadcasting Israel's entry
why: Télé Liban could not air the Israeli song under Lebanese law; EBU fined it and banned it for three years.

title: Lebanon beat France 74-73 at the basketball World Championship
why: One of the team's two wins in Japan; 17th place overall.

title: NYT puts Beirut first on its 44 places to go
why: Image rebound for a city; tourism hit about 2 million arrivals that year.

title: Tourism reaches about 2 million arrivals, up 39%
why: Beat the 1974 record; 2010 topped out at 2,351,081.

title: Lebanese NGO cooks a 233 kg kibbeh for a Guinness record
why: First shot in the food-record contest with Israel that became known as the hummus wars.

title: Beirut chefs serve a 10,452 kg hummus plate, a Guinness record
why: Chef Ramzi Choueiri and 300 cooks doubled the earlier 4-ton record held by Israel; a tabbouleh record (3,557 kg) followed in 2010.

title: Tourist arrivals hit a record 2,351,081
why: The highest figure in this series before the Syrian war and the crisis years.

title: Nadine Labaki wins Cannes Jury Prize for Capernaum
why: Film shot in Beirut slums; later an Oscar nominee (Jan 2019), first from an Arab woman director.

title: Lebanon play their first qualified AFC Asian Cup
why: Earlier, in 2000, the team took part as host; in 2019 it qualified on merit.

title: A USD 0.20 daily WhatsApp call charge lights the 17 October protests
why: The VoIP fee was withdrawn within hours, but it sparked a national movement over corruption and services.

title: A 171 km human chain links Tripoli to Tyre
why: Tens of thousands held hands along the coast; one of the most photographed images of the uprising.

title: Banks Association sets a USD 1,000 weekly withdrawal limit
why: Informal capital controls made official; limits fell to a few hundred dollars and then to zero in dollars.

title: Economist Dan Azzi coins "lollar" for trapped dollars
why: Deposits that show as dollars but cannot be withdrawn as such; later a Transparency Association protest printed mock lollar notes (May 2022). Page: Dan Azzi coined 'lollar'; LTA mock notes 13 May 2022; year of coinage not stated on page.

title: Dollar passes 3,000 pounds on the street
why: Two years after the Economist showed a Lebanese Big Mac at USD 4.30.

title: A 2,500 LBP loaf eats 11% of the minimum wage
why: Bread price rose 250 LBP twice in a month; monthly minimum wage quoted as 650,000.

title: Bread bundle shrinks and costs more: 385 g for 1,500 LBP
why: Weights cut as prices rose, the start of the subsidy unwind.

title: BDL launches the Sayrafa exchange platform
why: Another rate added to the list of rates Lebanese had to track; settled at 89,500 in Dec 2023.

title: Generator subscription doubles to 1,000,000 LBP for 5 A
why: Operators blamed black-market diesel; the generator owners' head is Abdo Saadeh.

title: Fuel queues and army raids on hoarders
why: Gas-station lines lasted hours; the army seized 78,000 l of petrol at two stations; at least one person was shot dead in a queue row.

title: Whole country goes dark as two power plants run out of fuel
why: Zahrani and Deir Ammar stopped; the army supplied emergency fuel.

title: A full tank now costs more than the monthly minimum wage
why: Al Jazeera: fuel subsidy lifted in June; station traffic fell from 200 cars a day to 30-40.

title: ABC News profiles the "generator mafia"
why: Owners of about 4,000 generators carve neighbourhoods into territories and set their own prices.

title: Depositors start storming banks to take their own money
why: Copycat hold-ups spread through the year; no robber had been prosecuted by Nov 2022.

title: Bread queues return as Ukraine war cuts wheat
why: No wheat orders since the war began; bakery queues and fights followed.

title: Transparency Association prints mock "lollar" notes
why: Six fantasy notes by painter Tom Young, a satirical currency of corruption.

title: Bassam al-Sheikh Hussein holds up a Hamra bank and gets USD 35,000
why: Seven hours with a rifle and petrol; crowds cheered outside; he wanted about USD 210,000 for his father's care.

title: Sali Hafez takes USD 13,000 from a Beirut bank with a toy gun
why: Needed for her sister's cancer treatment; five to eight hold-ups happened that day and banks shut for three days.

title: Banks close for three days as hold-ups spread
why: The ABL closed branches after multiple same-day hold-ups.

title: Mobile prices switch to dollars
why: Touch and Alfa cut the state-set SIM price to USD 3 and sold cards in dollars.

title: Private schools demand part of tuition in fresh dollars
why: USD 400-600 per pupil on top of about 9 million LBP at many schools, despite a law requiring LBP.

title: Coins become worthless
why: Wikipedia: by January 2023 no coins are used any more.

title: Reuters: cash is king, Lebanese carry bricks of 100,000 notes
why: Restaurant bill holders cannot hold the notes; billboards advertise note-counting machines.

title: Official rate reset from 1,507.5 to 15,000
why: First change to the official rate in 25 years; the dollar was already worth far more on the street.

title: Supermarkets start pricing goods in dollars
why: Shelf prices in USD, change in LBP; dollar rates on the street made quoting in pounds impractical.

title: Lebanon runs three exchange rates at once
why: Tax and VAT: 15,000 official, 85,500 Sayrafa and about 90,000 parallel; VAT used three rates along the supply chain.

title: Sayrafa rate is fixed at 89,500 LBP/USD
why: The stable rate since; today's price tables convert at this.

title: Tourist arrivals fall 32% to 1.13 million
why: From about 1.66 million in 2023, per a search summary of Tourism Ministry data.

title: Parliament approves LBP 500,000 to 5 million banknotes
why: So Lebanese can stop carrying wads of cash; printing expected to take about a year.

title: Ziad Rahbani dies; Fairuz attends the funeral on 28 July
why: Composer and playwright, son of Fairuz and Assi Rahbani; crowds gathered outside BMG Hospital.

title: Minimum wage raised to LBP 28 million, about USD 312
why: From 18 million; the wage was 675,000 (USD 450) in 2012 and USD 72 in the worst of the crisis.

title: Perla Harb crowned Miss Lebanon 2025
why: Ceremony at Zouk Mosbeh under the Ministry of Tourism, in a country that had lost Georgina Rizk's era of glamour.

title: The 21st Beirut Marathon draws 15,000 runners from 38 countries
why: Theme: run from the end to the beginning so Lebanon stands tall.

title: Petrol 95 at LBP 1,384,000 per 20 litres
why: After a 24,000 cut; the last price before the 2026 surge.

title: Big Mac costs 480,000 LBP (USD 5.36)
why: Economist index: same local price as Jan 2025, at 89,550 LBP/USD. CSV: LBN 2026-07-01 local_price 480000, dollar_ex 89550, dollar_price 5.36.

title: Bread bundle rises to LBP 80,000
why: Up from 75,000; diesel is cited as 22% of baking cost; the price is about USD 0.89.

title: Petrol 95 hits LBP 2,845,000 per 20 litres, about USD 32
why: Double the December 2025 price; 98 octane 2,863,000.

title: Lebanon "Golden Age" begins to 1975
why: European and American jet set fill Beirut's hotels and clubs; Hamra Street called its Champs-Elysees. Hamra Street page dates its heyday to the 1960s-70s; 1955 start not confirmed.
